title: Question Type and Productivity: Delilah (11) and Bryanna (13)
summary: A foundational overview of program evaluation methods, covering logic models, theory of change, and how to frame evaluation questions. Ideal for teams new to formal evaluation practice. Discusses formative vs. summative evaluation and when to use each approach.

title: Case Review: 13 year old Renee
summary: Practical strategies for collecting high-quality data in nonprofit settings, including survey design, interview protocols, and managing data from multiple sites. Special focus on low-resource environments and volunteer data collectors.

title: Case Review: 11 year old Matthew
summary: A foundational overview of program evaluation methods, covering logic models, theory of change, and how to frame evaluation questions. Ideal for teams new to formal evaluation practice. Discusses formative vs. summative evaluation and when to use each approach.

title: Case Review: 9 year old Faith
summary: Practical strategies for collecting high-quality data in nonprofit settings, including survey design, interview protocols, and managing data from multiple sites. Special focus on low-resource environments and volunteer data collectors.

title: Case Review: 12 year old Lesly
summary: How to transform raw evaluation data into compelling narratives for funders, boards, and communities. Covers data visualization principles, report writing, and communicating findings to non-technical audiences.

title: Case Review: 14 year old Deavyn
summary: Organizational strategies for embedding continuous learning and evaluation into everyday practice. Discusses leadership buy-in, staff capacity building, and creating systems that support reflection and adaptation.

title: Question Type and Productivity: Bryanna (13)
summary: An exploration of how equity and inclusion principles can be embedded throughout the evaluation cycle, from question design to dissemination. Covers culturally responsive evaluation frameworks and community-engaged approaches.

title: The First Jane Doe in the Epstein case: S.G. (14)
summary: A practical deep-dive into survey design, covering question types, response scales, order effects, and how to increase response rates. Includes common mistakes and how to avoid them.

title: Recantation: Azul (13)
summary: How to identify, define, and measure meaningful program outcomes. Covers the difference between outputs, outcomes, and impact, and how to select appropriate indicators for each level.

title: "Stuck in the same cycle everyday" Ashley (14)
summary: A comprehensive guide to using focus groups as an evaluation tool. Covers recruitment, facilitation techniques, note-taking, and how to analyze and report qualitative data from group discussions.
